question: For a four-leg intersection evaluated under the one-year Crash Experience signal warrant, what crash thresholds apply and what two additional categories of conditions must also be satisfied?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Under Warrant 7 (Crash Experience), a four-leg intersection satisfies the one-year crash condition if the number of reported angle and pedestrian crashes in a 1-year period (all severities) equals or exceeds the four-leg threshold in Table 4C-2, or if the number of reported fatal-and-injury angle and pedestrian crashes in a 1-year period equals or exceeds the corresponding Table 4C-2 threshold. In addition to the crash-history criterion, two other categories of conditions must also be met: (A) an adequate trial of alternatives with satisfactory observance and enforcement has failed to reduce the crash frequency, and (C) a traffic-volume condition applying to each of any 8 hours of an average day. Note that the specific numeric threshold values in Table 4C-2 and the full text of the volume criterion (C) are not included in the evidence provided. Guidance (recommended): - "The need for a traffic control signal should be considered if an engineering study finds that all of the following criteria are met: A. Adequate trial of alternatives with satisfactory observance and enforcement has failed to reduce the crash frequency; and B. At least one of the following conditions applies to the reported crash history..." - For the one-year period specifically: "1. The number of reported angle crashes and pedestrian crashes within a 1-year period equals or exceeds the threshold number in Table 4C-2 for total angle crashes and pedestrian crashes (all severities); or 2. The number of reported fatal-and-injury angle crashes and pedestrian crashes within a 1-year period equals or exceeds the threshold number in Table 4C-2 for total fatal-and-injury angle crashes and pedestrian crashes." - The third criterion is a volume condition: "C. For each of any 8 hours of an average day, the ve..." (the remainder of this provision is truncated in the evidence provided). Options (permitted): - If the posted or statutory speed limit or the 85th-percentile speed on the major street exceeds 40 mph, or if the intersection lies within the built-up area of an isolated community of fewer than 10,000 population, the 56 percent volume columns in Table 4C-1 may be used in place of the 80 percent columns, and Tables 4C-4 and 4C-5 may be used in place of Tables 4C-2 and 4C-3 (Table 4C-4 provides the reduced one-year crash thresholds, with separate values for four-leg intersections). - Agencies may calibrate Highway Safety Manual (HSM) safety performance functions to their own crash data, or develop their own SPFs, and — when documented in the engineering study — may use agency-specific crash frequency values in place of the values in Tables 4C-2 through 4C-5. Citations: - Section 4C.08 Guidance §2 (p.661) - Section 4C.08 Option §5 (p.662) - Section 4C.08 Option §6 (p.663) - Section 4C.08 Support §1 (p.661) - Section 4C.08 Support §7 (p.663)
gold_answer: The thresholds are at least 5 all-severity angle/pedestrian crashes or at least 3 fatal-and-injury angle/pedestrian crashes. In addition, an adequate trial of alternatives must have failed, and the applicable 80-percent vehicular-volume or pedestrian-volume condition must be met for the required hours.
